content.comment_body: Hello! Does anyone have advice on setting up Gmail as an email account? I've tried previous suggestions here but couldn't get them to work. I appreciate any guidance!
You can try these settings: Server name: smtp.gmail.com Connection security: STARTTLS Port: 587 Login name: Your Gmail address Login password: Your Gmail password
I've already tried those settings, but it still didn't work for me.
Which firmware version does your [product_name] have?
The packaging indicates firmware version FW: V1.84.02.
You should update your firmware to the latest version. The update is available online for [product_name] devices and the service pack for [product_name] software.
Alright, I'll test this and report back. Thanks for your help!
Please keep in mind, the password needed isn't for your Gmail account, but the App Password generated by Google.

First, check for DNS (name resolution) issues. However, the email setup in [company_name]'s product seems incomplete. For example: a) SMTP server parameters can't be set without authentication, although typically authentication isn't required for unencrypted port 25. Why does [product_name] enforce this? b) Entering recipient email addresses with multiple dots in the domain part causes errors (e.g., user@industry.[company_name].com or user@mail.server.com are marked invalid, while user@server.com is accepted).

analysis.insight_summary: Users face ongoing challenges configuring Gmail as an email service with [company_name]'s device. Common concerns include incompatibility with Google app password requirements, unclear authentication instructions, and rigid validation that blocks some valid email addresses. Suggestions such as firmware updates and app passwords exist but aren't documented clearly, resulting in user frustration. The email functionality appears underdeveloped for practical needs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a straightforward setup process for Gmail, with standard configuration guidance and explicit instructions for unique requirements. They expect the product to handle diverse email address formats properly and to support current authentication methods reliably.
